title: Cornchaff (Adalu): Corn and Beans in Palm Oil
author: Imma Adamu (Immaculate Bites)
desc: Dried beans and boiled corn simmered with smoked turkey or fish, tomatoes, garlic, ginger, onion, crayfish, smoked paprika and palm oil — a one-pot corn and bean porridge.
longDesc: Adamu describes cornchaff as a one-pot corn and beans porridge enjoyed throughout West Africa and especially popular in Nigeria and Cameroon. Dried beans are soaked overnight or 6 to 8 hours, then pressure-cooked roughly 8 to 12 minutes or cooked about 1 to 1½ hours until tender. Corn, smoked turkey or fish, tomatoes, garlic, ginger, onion, crayfish, palm oil, paprika and seasoning go in with 2–3 cups or more of water or stock and simmer about 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
ingredients: 1 pound dried beans, any variety (or three 16-ounce cans of beans)
1 pound corn (sweet boiled corn or any kind)
1–2 cups smoked turkey, fish or chicken
steps: Soak the beans overnight or 6 to 8 hours.
Pressure-cook the beans roughly 8 to 12 minutes, or cook in a pot about 1 to 1½ hours until tender.
Add the corn, smoked turkey or fish, tomatoes, garlic, ginger, onion, crayfish, palm oil, paprika, salt, pepper and bouillon with 2–3 cups or more of water or stock.
chefTips: The only printed cue is beans ‘until tender’.
Use the pressure cooker for the beans if you have one — the page gives both times.
The page says ‘any variety’ of bean but its method mentions red and black beans.
commonMistakes: Letting the pot catch while it simmers.
Adding the spices before the beans are tender — the exact order is not printed on the page.
healthBenefits: Beans and corn together give protein and fibre; palm oil adds fat.
culturalNote: The page says cornchaff is especially popular in Nigeria and Cameroon and names no region or community. The name appears as ‘cornchaff’, ‘corn tchap’ and ‘adalu’ in different sources.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Cornchaff (Adalu)’. Byline as printed: ‘Imma Adamu’. Published 20 Jan 2017, last updated 15 May 2021. Yield 6–8. Prep 1 h 30, cook 1 h 30, total 3 h. TWO-PASS; the exact order of additions after the beans is not captured, so the third step follows the ingredient list.
As printed: ‘1 teaspoons’ ginger; the first pass noted the method mentions red and black beans while the list says any variety.
